Implement m3a-009 in the real Tokage repository. Search currently filters matching attempts but leaves their provider/model groups collapsed, making results invisible. When the trimmed search query is nonempty, render matching provider/model groups expanded regardless of saved collapse preference. On clearing via clear button or Escape, restore the exact previous manual expansion preferences. While search is active, do not allow group toggle clicks to hide matching results or mutate saved preferences; expose expanded and disabled state on native toggles while searching. Whitespace-only query is normal unfiltered mode. Preserve native aria-controls/current/pressed semantics and unique stable IDs from m3a-008. Keep selection/transcript and IPC readers independent of search; do not alter poller/store/IPC or introduce dependency changes. Add actual rendered SessionHistoryView tests with real pollHistory. Preserve every existing regression unchanged. Edit only writeScope, no .tokage/docs/runner/build/auth/model/DB/config or Git config changes. Independent exact-head review and desktop UI merge downstream.

I'll start by checking the workspace state, the two environment variables you asked me to inspect, and the shared task context.

The component is clear. Next I'll check the shared context file (its earlier read failed), the existing SessionHistoryView tests, the poller, and the package scripts.

Key constraints from this read: the existing `SessionHistoryView.test.tsx` mocks `historyPoller`, so my new test file must not mock it. Next I'll read the remaining SessionHistoryView tests and the Vitest config to see how they're set up.

The HEAD commit contains an archived prior attempt for this task (`attempt-1`), which may show why it failed. Before that, I'll start the offline dependency install in the background using the workspace-seeded npm cache and TMPDIR, as the brief specifies.

The archived attempt was blocked for writing HOME memory files and npm default logs, so I'll keep both out of scope. I won't reuse that candidate patch; I'll build from the current source. Next I'll check the Vitest/Vite config, the i18n check, and the IPC signatures the tests mock.

The install finished cleanly (258 packages, exit 0). Next I'll start a baseline full test run in the background, so I know the pre-change state, and read the Vite config while it runs.

The Vite config has no test block, so Vitest uses its defaults plus the per-file `happy-dom` pragma. Before writing tests, I'll check three things: whether typecheck covers test files, the English strings the tests will match, and the baseline run's progress.

Baseline `npm test` passed (exit 0). The tsconfig includes `src`, so the new test file gets typechecked too. Next I'll pull the baseline summary and the English UI strings the tests will match.

Baseline: 50 files, 353 tests, all passing. Next I'll pull the English strings for the session-history keys I'll match in tests.

I have what I need for the design. Before touching the component, I'll write the regression tests first (per the CLAUDE.md "reproduce, then fix" rule) and confirm they fail on the current code. The new test file renders the real component and uses the real `pollHistory`, mocking only the IPC functions.

The test file is written. Next I'll run it against the unchanged component to confirm the new behavior is actually missing (the red phase).

The red phase behaves as intended: the three behavior tests fail on the current code (matches stay hidden under collapsed groups). Tests 4 and 5 pass only because they check the post-clear state, so I'll add during-search assertions to them. Then I'll re-run to confirm they fail too.

Now the component fix. The change is small: derive `searchActive` from the trimmed query, make matching groups render expanded while it is true (saved preferences are never written during search), and disable the native toggles. I'll apply the edits one at a time to the same file.

All five component edits are in. Next I'll run the new test file (green phase) and the existing SessionHistoryView suites to check that the original regressions still pass unchanged.

All 7 SessionHistoryView files pass (30 tests). Next I'll check the output for React `act` or other warnings that a passing run could hide, and confirm the new test file's own results.

All 8 new tests pass with no `act` or console warnings. Before running the full acceptance chain, I'll review the component diff and check whether the production build writes an ignored `dist/` directory, so I know whether to clean up afterward.

The diff is minimal: one derived flag, effective expansion for matching groups while the query is non-blank, and `disabled` on both native toggles. `dist/` is already gitignored. Next I'll run the full acceptance chain from the brief: offline install with the workspace cache, typecheck, full tests, i18n check, and production build.

Full suite passes: 51 files and 361 tests (baseline was 50 and 353, so the +8 are the new tests). The i18n check also passes. Last acceptance step is the production build.

Build passes (exit 0). The warnings it prints are about unrelated modules (`appendTriage.ts`, `taskRunner.ts`, chunk size), not this change. Next is a mutation check: I'll temporarily restore the HEAD component, confirm the new tests fail, then restore my fix from a backup and confirm the diff is unchanged.

The mutation check behaves as intended: on the original component, 5 of the 8 new tests fail (the exposure, toggle, both clear-path, and polling behaviors). The other 3 pass on both versions and act as regression guards. The fix is restored and the component diff is back to 6 insertions and 2 deletions.

One correction before wrapping up: the comment above `collapseMixed` describes the wrong groups. I'll fix it to match what the helper actually does.

Now I'll confirm the restored component matches my fix byte-for-byte, delete the scratch backup, and re-run the full acceptance chain on the final state. I'm re-running even though the last edit was only a comment, so the reported results match what's on disk.

m3a-009 is implemented and verified in the worktree. Nothing is committed, per the brief.

## 结果

- **组件（`SessionHistoryView.tsx`）**：去掉首尾空白后非空即视为搜索生效。生效时，匹配的 provider/model 分组渲染为展开，两级原生切换按钮加上 `disabled`。搜索期间不写入保存的偏好，因此清空（清除按钮或 Escape）后原样恢复，无需额外的快照代码。纯空白查询保持普通模式。
- **测试（新增 `SessionHistoryView.searchExpansion.test.tsx`）**：8 个渲染 DOM 的测试，使用真实 `pollHistory`，仅 mock IPC 读取。
- **红绿验证**：先写测试。在原组件上运行，8 个中 5 个失败（匹配项不可见、切换可点、清空后的恢复、轮询）；其余 3 个是回归守卫（纯空白、零匹配、选中与 IPC），在两个版本上都通过。修复后 8 个全部通过。
- **验收链**（workspace 缓存 + `TMPDIR`）：`npm ci` 离线成功；typecheck 通过；`npm test` 51 个文件 / 361 个测试通过（基线 353）；`check:i18n` 通过；build 通过（警告针对无关模块，如 `appendTriage`、`taskRunner` 和 chunk 大小）。
- **范围**：`git status` 只有两个文件。原有测试未改动。

### 执行计划与验证

| 步骤 | 验证方式 | 结果 |
|---|---|---|
| 只检查两个环境变量 | 只输出这两个变量 | `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1`；`npm_config_cache` 指向夹具临时目录 |
| 离线安装 | `npm ci --cache ./src-tauri/target/m3a-npm-cache --offline --ignore-scripts` | 258 个包，exit 0 |
| 基线 | `npm test` | 353 通过 |
| 红灯测试 | 对原组件运行新测试 | 5/8 失败，符合预期 |
| 修复 | 同上 + 全量验收 | 全部通过 |

### 说明与遗留

- 我的选择：搜索生效定义为 trim 后非空；禁用依赖原生 `disabled`，不加 JS 守卫（React 会忽略禁用按钮的点击）；未增加禁用态的视觉样式。
- **未做**：真实 CLAUDE_CODE / claude-haiku-5-5 桌面验收、独立 exact-head 审查、桌面 UI 合并。这些是下游门禁，超出我的 writeScope，我没有运行 runner。
- AGENTS.md 要求自动提交子节点，与 brief 的"不要自行提交"冲突，我按 brief 不提交。
- `.tokage/context.md` 在此 worktree 中不存在。

I'll start by checking the workspace state, the two environment variables you asked me to inspect, and the shared task context.

The component is clear. Next I'll check the shared context file (its earlier read failed), the existing SessionHistoryView tests, the poller, and the package scripts.

Key constraints from this read: the existing `SessionHistoryView.test.tsx` mocks `historyPoller`, so my new test file must not mock it. Next I'll read the remaining SessionHistoryView tests and the Vitest config to see how they're set up.

The HEAD commit contains an archived prior attempt for this task (`attempt-1`), which may show why it failed. Before that, I'll start the offline dependency install in the background using the workspace-seeded npm cache and TMPDIR, as the brief specifies.

The archived attempt was blocked for writing HOME memory files and npm default logs, so I'll keep both out of scope. I won't reuse that candidate patch; I'll build from the current source. Next I'll check the Vitest/Vite config, the i18n check, and the IPC signatures the tests mock.

The install finished cleanly (258 packages, exit 0). Next I'll start a baseline full test run in the background, so I know the pre-change state, and read the Vite config while it runs.

The Vite config has no test block, so Vitest uses its defaults plus the per-file `happy-dom` pragma. Before writing tests, I'll check three things: whether typecheck covers test files, the English strings the tests will match, and the baseline run's progress.

Baseline `npm test` passed (exit 0). The tsconfig includes `src`, so the new test file gets typechecked too. Next I'll pull the baseline summary and the English UI strings the tests will match.

Baseline: 50 files, 353 tests, all passing. Next I'll pull the English strings for the session-history keys I'll match in tests.

I have what I need for the design. Before touching the component, I'll write the regression tests first (per the CLAUDE.md "reproduce, then fix" rule) and confirm they fail on the current code. The new test file renders the real component and uses the real `pollHistory`, mocking only the IPC functions.

The test file is written. Next I'll run it against the unchanged component to confirm the new behavior is actually missing (the red phase).

The red phase behaves as intended: the three behavior tests fail on the current code (matches stay hidden under collapsed groups). Tests 4 and 5 pass only because they check the post-clear state, so I'll add during-search assertions to them. Then I'll re-run to confirm they fail too.

Now the component fix. The change is small: derive `searchActive` from the trimmed query, make matching groups render expanded while it is true (saved preferences are never written during search), and disable the native toggles. I'll apply the edits one at a time to the same file.

All five component edits are in. Next I'll run the new test file (green phase) and the existing SessionHistoryView suites to check that the original regressions still pass unchanged.

All 7 SessionHistoryView files pass (30 tests). Next I'll check the output for React `act` or other warnings that a passing run could hide, and confirm the new test file's own results.

All 8 new tests pass with no `act` or console warnings. Before running the full acceptance chain, I'll review the component diff and check whether the production build writes an ignored `dist/` directory, so I know whether to clean up afterward.

The diff is minimal: one derived flag, effective expansion for matching groups while the query is non-blank, and `disabled` on both native toggles. `dist/` is already gitignored. Next I'll run the full acceptance chain from the brief: offline install with the workspace cache, typecheck, full tests, i18n check, and production build.

Full suite passes: 51 files and 361 tests (baseline was 50 and 353, so the +8 are the new tests). The i18n check also passes. Last acceptance step is the production build.

Build passes (exit 0). The warnings it prints are about unrelated modules (`appendTriage.ts`, `taskRunner.ts`, chunk size), not this change. Next is a mutation check: I'll temporarily restore the HEAD component, confirm the new tests fail, then restore my fix from a backup and confirm the diff is unchanged.

The mutation check behaves as intended: on the original component, 5 of the 8 new tests fail (the exposure, toggle, both clear-path, and polling behaviors). The other 3 pass on both versions and act as regression guards. The fix is restored and the component diff is back to 6 insertions and 2 deletions.

One correction before wrapping up: the comment above `collapseMixed` describes the wrong groups. I'll fix it to match what the helper actually does.

Now I'll confirm the restored component matches my fix byte-for-byte, delete the scratch backup, and re-run the full acceptance chain on the final state. I'm re-running even though the last edit was only a comment, so the reported results match what's on disk.

m3a-009 is implemented and verified in the worktree. Nothing is committed, per the brief.

## 结果

- **组件（`SessionHistoryView.tsx`）**：去掉首尾空白后非空即视为搜索生效。生效时，匹配的 provider/model 分组渲染为展开，两级原生切换按钮加上 `disabled`。搜索期间不写入保存的偏好，因此清空（清除按钮或 Escape）后原样恢复，无需额外的快照代码。纯空白查询保持普通模式。
- **测试（新增 `SessionHistoryView.searchExpansion.test.tsx`）**：8 个渲染 DOM 的测试，使用真实 `pollHistory`，仅 mock IPC 读取。
- **红绿验证**：先写测试。在原组件上运行，8 个中 5 个失败（匹配项不可见、切换可点、清空后的恢复、轮询）；其余 3 个是回归守卫（纯空白、零匹配、选中与 IPC），在两个版本上都通过。修复后 8 个全部通过。
- **验收链**（workspace 缓存 + `TMPDIR`）：`npm ci` 离线成功；typecheck 通过；`npm test` 51 个文件 / 361 个测试通过（基线 353）；`check:i18n` 通过；build 通过（警告针对无关模块，如 `appendTriage`、`taskRunner` 和 chunk 大小）。
- **范围**：`git status` 只有两个文件。原有测试未改动。

### 执行计划与验证

| 步骤 | 验证方式 | 结果 |
|---|---|---|
| 只检查两个环境变量 | 只输出这两个变量 | `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1`；`npm_config_cache` 指向夹具临时目录 |
| 离线安装 | `npm ci --cache ./src-tauri/target/m3a-npm-cache --offline --ignore-scripts` | 258 个包，exit 0 |
| 基线 | `npm test` | 353 通过 |
| 红灯测试 | 对原组件运行新测试 | 5/8 失败，符合预期 |
| 修复 | 同上 + 全量验收 | 全部通过 |

### 说明与遗留

- 我的选择：搜索生效定义为 trim 后非空；禁用依赖原生 `disabled`，不加 JS 守卫（React 会忽略禁用按钮的点击）；未增加禁用态的视觉样式。
- **未做**：真实 CLAUDE_CODE / claude-haiku-5-5 桌面验收、独立 exact-head 审查、桌面 UI 合并。这些是下游门禁，超出我的 writeScope，我没有运行 runner。
- AGENTS.md 要求自动提交子节点，与 brief 的"不要自行提交"冲突，我按 brief 不提交。
- `.tokage/context.md` 在此 worktree 中不存在。
- 上一次尝试（`attempt-1`）因写入 HOME 记忆文件和 npm 默认日志被阻断。本次未复用其候选补丁，也未主动写入 HOME 或记忆路径。一条诊断命令（`npx --no-install vitest`）未带 `--cache`，使用了夹具提供的缓存路径（位于 HOME 与 worktree 之外）。
- 既有风险（未改动）：分组键以 `::` 拼接，若 CLI 或模型名包含 `::`，键和 `aria-controls` ID 会冲突。
- 无人工协助。失败仅为计划内的红灯测试。

originalRequest:
Implement m3a-009 in the real Tokage repository. Search currently filters matching attempts but leaves their provider/model groups collapsed, making results invisible. When the trimmed search query is nonempty, render matching provider/model groups expanded regardless of saved collapse preference. On clearing via clear button or Escape, restore the exact previous manual expansion preferences. While search is active, do not allow group toggle clicks to hide matching results or mutate saved preferences; expose expanded and disabled state on native toggles while searching. Whitespace-only query is normal unfiltered mode. Preserve native aria-controls/current/pressed semantics and unique stable IDs from m3a-008. Keep selection/transcript and IPC readers independent of search; do not alter poller/store/IPC or introduce dependency changes. Add actual rendered SessionHistoryView tests with real pollHistory. Preserve every existing regression unchanged. Edit only writeScope, no .tokage/docs/runner/build/auth/model/DB/config or Git config changes. Host commits using default identity and built-in coauthor: do not commit yourself. Use seeded per-workspace npm cache and ignored src-tauri/target/m3a-tmp TMPDIR; run all commands and report required TaskReport headings (deviations None if none). Independent exact-head review and desktop UI merge downstream.

Preregistered acceptance:
With both provider and model groups manually collapsed, entering a matching task ID/model/role/status query exposes actual matching attempt buttons through non-hidden ancestors. Both levels aria-expanded=true, native toggles disabled during active search; toggle attempts do not hide results or alter saved preferences. Whitespace-only query does not force expansion.
Clearing with the existing clear button or Escape restores exact pre-search per-provider/model expansion preferences, including mixed collapsed/expanded groups. Focus returns/stays in search input. Searching does not change the selected attempt or transcript and does not directly trigger extra IPC reads. Selection semantics remain correct after results return.
Polling updates while searching keep current matches visible without losing saved preferences. New groups default expanded; existing preferences survive search with zero matches and later clear. Stable unique aria-controls remain valid and no hidden descendant becomes improperly exposed. Test actual rendered DOM and real pollHistory, not helper-only assertions.
All original tests unchanged, full frontend tests/typecheck/i18n/production build pass. Only the two scoped files changed; no dependency/config/Git identity/poller/store/IPC/model/auth/DB changes. Real CLAUDE_CODE/claude-haiku-5-5 durable DONE and actual model evidence, all task/delivery gates and independent exact-head review before desktop UI merge; archive all failures and assistance.
Fixture environment disables automatic memory and redirects npm_config_cache to the marked temporary root. Do not create or update any memory files or HOME files. Before execution, inspect only CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY and npm_config_cache (never dump environment/secrets); preserve the seeded workspace cache for offline install. No business requirements or scope have changed.
Environment repaired and independently verified: each worktree receives an independent writable npm cache at src-tauri/target/m3a-npm-cache. Use npm --cache ./src-tauri/target/m3a-npm-cache for installs, with --offline --ignore-scripts; happy-dom@21.0.3 and this project dependencies are seeded. For test commands, create src-tauri/target/m3a-tmp and set TMPDIR="$PWD/src-tauri/target/m3a-tmp". These paths are already ignored. Do not write HOME or relax sandbox policy. Actually render SessionHistoryView in a DOM regression; do not replace this with EventTarget-only tests or omit tests because the previous shared cache failed.

m3a-009.rawOutput:
The failing command is the literal acceptance install, which has no `--cache` flag. The error log is under the fixture cache, so npm used the harness-provided `npm_config_cache` rather than the per-workspace cache. I'll confirm that with read-only checks: which cache holds the `zwitch-2.0.4` tarball the lockfile needs, and what the fixture cache contains. I'm not touching the fixture cache.

Both caches show 456 index files and no index hit for the URL. That doesn't settle it, because npm can read tarballs from the content store by integrity without an index entry. I'll check the lockfile integrity hash against the content store in each cache.

The `zwitch-2.0.4` blob exists in both content stores, and both hold 451 blobs. So this is not a missing-tarball problem. npm's URL-keyed request cache has no entry for that URL in either cache. Because my `--cache` install succeeded, that URL path must be what fails under the fixture env.

Before drawing a conclusion, I'll re-run the literal acceptance command exactly as written in this environment. It is the spec being gated, and the fixture cache may have been seeded after the harness's failed run. If it fails again, the `--cache` install below is the fallback. The brief sets TMPDIR for test commands, so I'll set it here too.

The literal acceptance chain now passes in this worktree: `npm ci` without `--cache` added 258 packages, and typecheck, tests (361 passed), i18n and build all completed. The harness's failure is therefore not reproducible here. Before writing that up, I'll check read-only whether the fixture cache changed between the harness's failure (00:53:04Z) and now, since that is the only candidate explanation.

The fixture cache has not changed since before the harness failure: nothing in its index or content stores is newer than 00:53:04Z, and its seeding dates from Oct 20. The cache is not the explanation. The harness log's own header lines should show the working directory and argv it used. I'll grep only for those fields, not the whole log.

The harness log settles the environment question: same worktree, same argv, same npm (11.4.2). The sequence for zwitch is a cache hit, then "no local data ... Extracting by manifest," then ENOTCACHED. That means npm's content-by-integrity lookup missed in that run. I'll compare the zwitch lines in the harness log with the same lines from my successful `npm ci` log, which should be the first of the 00:56 logs.

This is the actual difference. In the failing run, npm reported "no local data for zwitch … Extracting by manifest," meaning the lookup by lockfile integrity missed. In my passing run, that line is absent and npm went straight to ADD. The blob was written on Oct 20 and has not changed since, so the miss must come from the lookup input, most likely the lockfile's integrity value at 00:53. I'll check whether `package-lock.json` or the worktree HEAD changed after the harness run.

The lockfile has not changed since the worktree was created at 08:44, before the harness run, and npm is the same 11.4.2 version. So the lockfile and tooling are ruled out.
